proof_review.household_timing: Read full household section. Saving-unit a and payoff-unit b linked only at constant q. Worst-path discounted budget requires R>1 and admissible permanent low income; equality permits zero consumption. Continuous Euler perturbation and stationary marginal-utility integration retain integrability/no-upper-cap assumptions and are not asserted on the grid.
proof_review.precautionary_comparison: For common feasible interval and positive consumption, strict concavity gives decreasing derivative; convex marginal utility shifts it upward under convex order. Endpoints handled by signs, strictness conditional. Cases independently solved by bisection rather than author radicals.
proof_review.finite_verification: Finite feasible positive consumptions imply bounded reward; max contraction, Cauchy iteration, fixed-point uniqueness, and telescoped bounded terminal value establish all-history/randomized optimality. Residual and fixed-policy inverse arguments valid. Peer uses value iteration and discounted reward sum, not author linear-solve/policy enumeration.
proof_review.joint_distribution: Cesaro compactness proves existence only. Minorization decomposition, signed-row norm contraction, uniqueness of m-step law, commuting one-step invariance and remainder nonexpansion prove convergence, including epsilon=1. Residual certificate and bounded-statistic half-span bound valid. Positive income transition need not mix wealth classes.
proof_review.exchange_and_production: Every action compared and full joint distribution propagated. Exchange bonds net to zero. In production, factors come from stated CRS technology and wealth owns capital; zero profits prevent double-counted dividends. Exact finite capital/goods/labor closure does not establish continuous-asset existence.
proof_review.aggregation: Constrained two-date policy derives from concavity and lower-bound sign. Equal mean but different distribution changes next mean. Affine aggregation formula is exact without independence; nonlinear policy lacks that closure.
proof_review.price_and_numerics: Finite two-date common deterministic rule has no clearing price; explicit indifferent heterogeneous choices clear. Separate infinite-horizon linear-utility example has a valid identity-policy equilibrium although a selected tie rule has no root. Operator error requires common domain; transition perturbation uses telescoping and minorization. Mesh comparison and sign change are not existence/error proofs.
